I'll read the batch-9 script and doc and fix the rollback header plus the four review nits.The rollback block is missing its run-header, and the script still has the four review gaps. I'll add the header and those guards only.**Detail**

The Rollback blocker is cleared. The first fenced block under `## Rollback` in `docs/cis-fix/batch-9.md` now starts with `# RUNS ON: JOHNNY (SSH)`. The other fenced blocks already had a run header.

The four review notes are in `docs/cis-fix/batch-9.sh`, plus the one doc line the review asked for.

- Right after `CHANGED=1`, PASTE 1 sets `trap 'trap - ERR HUP; echo ERR-REVERT; bash "$REVERT"' ERR HUP`. An unguarded failure (`chage`, `useradd -D`, `mkdir`, `sed`, `systemd-run`, and the same class of command) runs `/root/batch9-revert.sh` before the shell exits. `HUP` is on that same trap so a dropped SSH session does the same restore. The trap clears itself first so a failing revert does not call itself again. Explicit `bash "$REVERT"` paths are unchanged.
- The Plan section has one new line, ahead of the PASTE 2 instructions: if `TIMER-ARMED` is not printed, run `sudo bash /root/batch9-revert.sh`.
- PASTE 2 and PASTE 3 now check `systemctl is-active --quiet johnny-cis-batch9-revert.service` before they touch the timer. If that service is already active they print `STOP-revert-running` and exit. They no longer stop the service, so a timer that fires at the edge of 300 seconds is not killed mid-extract.
- `policy_files_ok` now requires `passwd -S aj` field 5 (maximum) to be `365` and field 7 (inactive) to be `45`. A later run that finds the files already written but aging not applied does not print `OK-batch-9`.
- `active_eq` and `active_bare` write a newline before appending when the file is non-empty and does not already end with one.

`bash -n docs/cis-fix/batch-9.sh` completed with exit 0. Nothing has been run on Johnny. No commit.
